claims.text: DIA's covering letter of 22 August 1996 to John Greenewald states that 'A search of DIA's systems of records located one document responsive to the subject of your request', released 'with only administrative markings withheld'.

claims.nodeLabel: Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 intercepts, Tehran, 19-20 September 1976
claims.sourceText: DIA IR 6 846 0139 76, released under FOIA case U-80,597/PO/FOIA, https://www.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/1976iranincident.pdf
claims.text: The report is IR 6 846 0139 76 from USDAO Tehran to DIA Washington, DTG 230530Z SEP 76, subject 'REPORTED UFO SIGHTING (U)', country Iran, dates '19 & 20 SEP 76', prepared by Frank B. McKenzie, Col, USAF, Defense Attache, and distributed to CJCS, the Joint Staff, NMCC, SECDEF, NMIC, State, CIA, NSA, the White House, CMC, CSAF, CNO and CSA.

claims.nodeLabel: Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 intercepts, Tehran, 19-20 September 1976
claims.text: The report names no Iranian aircrew. Its own comments field reads: 'ACTUAL INFORMATION CONTAINED IN THIS REPORT WAS OBTAINED FROM SOURCE IN CONVERSATION WITH A SUB-SOURCE, AND IIAF PILOT OF ONE OF THE F-4S. MORE INFORMATION WILL BE FORWARDED WHEN IT BECOMES AVAILABLE.'

claims.nodeLabel: Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 intercepts, Tehran, 19-20 September 1976
claims.sourceText: DIA IR 6 846 0139 76, page 4, with the DIA FOIA response of 22 August 1996, https://www.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/1976iranincident.pdf
claims.text: The report states that 'THE AIRCRAFT AND AREA WHERE THE OBJECT IS BELIEVED TO HAVE LANDED ARE BEING CHECKED FOR POSSIBLE RADIATION'; no result of that check is in DIA's release, and DIA's 1996 search located no further document.

claims.nodeLabel: Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 intercepts, Tehran, 19-20 September 1976
claims.text: The report records that the command post called BG Yousefi, Assistant Deputy Commander of Operations, who decided to scramble an F-4 from Shahrokhi AFB; that at a range of 25 nm the first aircraft 'LOST ALL INSTRUMENTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS (UHF AND INTERCOM)' and broke off; and that a second F-4 launched at 0140 hrs acquired a radar lock at 27 nm before its pilot 'ATTEMPTED TO FIRE AN AIM-9 MISSILE AT THE OBJECT BUT AT THAT INSTANT HIS WEAPONS CONTROL PANEL WENT OFF'.
